topics.title: [eval] Check in the September evaluation campaign
topics.body:
Check in the model, evaluator, and launcher configurations for the September 2026 evaluation campaign, together with the runtime fixes needed for serving, retry, resume, and coverage. The launcher validates external pins, writes immutable effective-config snapshots, and accepts an optional submitter-controlled version label. That label does not attest policy conformance.

Harbor results are bound to the full model and hosted judge configurations, dataset, policy, runtime, and task limit. Resume checks this identity before submission and reuse. A changed checkpoint under the same served name is rejected, as are existing roots without model-bound provenance. Recovery retries known infrastructure failures and unscored trials while retaining scored outcomes and unknown errors.

The frozen Harbor runtime pins 94b118022fe3e677784a638daf33d57a836fa5fe and includes the Tau3 adapter. The Evalchemy lock and generated pin match Marin's external dependency configuration.

SWE-bench uses the native Mini-SWE adapter from merged [Harbor #232](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/232) and [#233](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/233). Its 32,768-token context includes the prompt and reply together. Mini-SWE counts the rendered prompt through the serving tokenizer, including tools and the generation prefix, and caps the reply within the remaining budget and server window. Harbor loads Mini-SWE's base configuration before applying overrides and selects its batch agent, which saves the trajectory on context exhaustion without prompting. Harbor can then verify the existing patch.

Sotopia uses the packaged agent from merged [Harbor #231](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/231). Judge failures become verifier infrastructure errors. The Marin agent wrappers and their harness dependencies are removed. Sotopia's native generation still does not enforce its declared context budget, so those results cannot establish conformance to the 32K context policy.

topics.title: [levanter] Add a benchmark for the Triton ragged_dot kernels
topics.body:
Add `lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_ragged_dot_triton.py`, which times the Triton grouped GEMM behind `haliax.nn.ragged_dot` on one GPU. For each layout (fwd, dlhs, drhs) it times both Triton kernel families (`tile_map` and `group_grid`), XLA's `ragged_dot_general` and a dense `jnp.matmul` with the same FLOPs. Each timing is the median of repeated windows after a warmup. Rows are written as JSON lines.

With `--sweep`, the script times the tile-map kernel for every block config in a bounded grid. `--shard i/n` runs every n-th config, so the GPUs of one node can split the grid. The AMD block-size table and the per-call numbers in #9859 came from this script on MI350X.

The script imports the tile-map kernels added in #9859, so this PR targets that branch. Merge #9859 first.

topics.title: [grug] Correct hero remat and collective scheduling; build PGLE profiles
topics.body:
Carry-offloaded hero runs stop recomputing ~10 GiB of backward values per step that already fit in HBM, which shortens the step by 1.04% (13.874 to 13.732 s against #9830 on one 64-GPU hero rack, restore step-180000, seed 0, 100 steps). Ragged runs without the carry offload run their collectives one at a time, and `pgle_profile` builds an XLA PGLE profile from one trace of the train step. No model code changes.

With the layer carry offloaded to pinned host memory, XLA's `HloRematerialization` charged the 36 GiB carry stack against the device memory limit and recomputed values that fit (143 remat clones, 0.63 s/step of compute). The launcher now defaults `--xla_gpu_enable_host_memory_offloading=true` whenever the carry is offloaded, so remat counts host buffers as host memory. Only the remat pass reads the flag, after scheduling and copy insertion, so it cannot reorder the carry reload against its consumer. The flag also lets remat offload values to host itself when its estimate of the step exceeds its budget, and that path aborts compilation in XLA's `OffloadInstruction` (hlo_rematerialization.cc:2118) when it picks the operand of a collective still in flight. At memory fraction 0.75 and slop factor 85 the budget is 87.7 GiB and remat estimates the step at 96.8 GiB, so the hero crashed at compile. The carry offload therefore also defaults to 0.78 and 105, a 114 GiB budget, and remat then leaves the step alone ("Rematerialized 0 instructions").

A ragged run without the carry offload keeps the latency-hiding scheduler off, and the collective overlap limit binds only that scheduler, so XLA's default scheduler can start two ragged transports at once. Compiled for a mocked EP64 topology, the program does so in the forward and in the backward, and on GB200 several collectives in flight have hung the ragged transport or given run-to-run different gradients. The launcher now forces `--xla_gpu_disable_async_collectives=ALLCOLLECTIVES` for that configuration.

XLA's default latency estimator gives every collective the same small latency, so with one collective in flight it treats a multi-millisecond ragged transport as hidden under one GEMM. A profile built by `pgle_profile` from the program's own trace shortened the hero step with all of #9708 from 12.611 to 12.515 s (+0.77%). A profile applies only to the program it was traced from, so nothing uses one by default; the README describes the trace, build and rerun loop, and #9879 tracks using one in production.

Split from #9708. Part of #9636.

Non-target retention was not evaluated. Historical calibration tensors and raw evaluation transcripts remain private, so refitting/rerunning is supported but exact calibrated-output replay is not guaranteed.

topics.title: [grug] Let the hero launch use the carry-offload memory budget
topics.body:
`trigger_hero.sh` passed `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.75` and `--xla_gpu_memory_limit_slop_factor=85` to the hero coordinator. Since #9831, `_apply_hero_ep_runtime_defaults` gives the hero's carry-offload configuration a 0.78 memory fraction and slop factor 105 together with `--xla_gpu_enable_host_memory_offloading`. Explicit values take precedence over those defaults, and `run_grug` copies the coordinator environment into the training tasks, so a hero launched from main would compile with 0.75 / 85 and host-memory offloading on. On one GB200 rack restoring the hero's step-180000 checkpoint, that combination aborts compilation on every rank in `HloRematerialization` (`hlo_rematerialization.cc:2118`, `Check failed: !place_before_list.empty()`).

Without the two overrides the launch resolves to 0.78 / 105 with host-memory offloading, the configuration measured in the #9831–#9834 rack benchmarks. The live hero is unaffected: Iris retries reuse the bundle it was launched with.

Follow-up to #9831.

topics.title: [inference] Eval runner counts a Kueue-gated serve pod as placed and burns the startup budget while queued
topics.body:
`marin.inference.iris._wait_for_endpoint` (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py`) budgets serve startup with `ENDPOINT_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (2,400 s) only while a task is placed, and queue time separately with a 4 h placement budget. It decides placement with `_PLACED_TASK_STATES = {ASSIGNED, BUILDING, RUNNING}`. The Iris k8s backend (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py`, Pending branch) reports every Pending pod as `TASK_STATE_BUILDING`, including a pod that Kueue holds behind a scheduling gate (status message starts with `SchedulingGated: Scheduling is blocked due to non-empty scheduling gates; Kueue workload …`). So a serve that is merely queued is treated as starting, and the evaluation fails with `Timed out waiting for inference endpoint` after 40 minutes while no GPU was ever allocated.

Observed 2026-10-11 on cw-rno2a (marin #9984): eval groups `/karan/eval-20261010-231346-gate-mixed-rs-lr1e-06-step364-dda9`, `/karan/eval-20261011-000224-gate-mixed-rs-lr1e-06-step546-0e65`, `/karan/eval-20261011-005242-gate-mixed-rs-lr1e-06-step727-b634` (and five more the same night): each serve child ended `killed` with task duration `-`, preemptions 0 and the SchedulingGated diagnostic; each eval task ran 40 min and recorded infra_failed.

Expected: a gated pod counts as queued (placement budget), and the startup budget starts only when the pod is scheduled (node assigned / container started). Done when: a serve held in a Kueue gate for longer than the startup budget still produces a successful evaluation once admitted, and a unit test covers gated → placed → requeued timing of the two budgets.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`_wait_for_endpoint()` treats every `BUILDING` task as placed. The Kubernetes backend reports a Pending pod as `BUILDING` before Kueue removes its scheduling gate, so the 2,400-second startup deadline can expire without a node assignment. No open PR overlaps this fix.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris.py#L539-L579`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py#L539-L579) - placement and deadline logic
- [`tasks.py#L1251-L1266`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L1251-L1266) - Pending pod state and node identity
- [`workload.py#L91-L127`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/client/workload.py#L91-L127) - exposed worker and node fields

# Proposed Fix

Kueue-gated Pending pod → `BUILDING` task → `_PLACED_TASK_STATES` → startup timeout. Count a task as placed only when its current attempt has a node, its Iris worker is assigned, or it is running; keep requeued tasks on the placement budget. Add a waiter regression test for gated → placed → requeued → admitted timing.

🤖 Fix proposed in #10038. The 2,400-second startup budget now starts only after the current attempt has a worker or node assignment, or the task runs; this ignores federated peer display labels and keeps gated pods on the four-hour placement budget. The regression covers gating, placement, requeue, and readmission; 95 evaluation tests and lint pass.

topics.title: [experiment] Snowball SFT on GLM-5.3 traces from Skill2Env biology tasks
topics.body:
## TL;DR

**Experiment finished on October 9, 2026.** Closing with no demonstrated improvement on the primary Pi/BixBench evaluation. The remaining uncertainties are recorded as limitations; no further training, evaluation, or investigation is planned under this issue.

The biology-only SFT run is complete, but the primary evaluation on **Pi**, the harness used to collect the teacher traces and intended for deployment, has not demonstrated improved BixBench performance. On five questions selected using historical runtime, **Pi with thinking enabled scored parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5**, with all attempts graded. The final response contained an unexecuted tool call in the parsed reasoning field in 1/5 parent attempts and 5/5 SFT attempts. The affected parent attempt had already written the correct answer and still received credit. Two SFT attempts executed no tools, while three executed tools before that ending. This failure therefore also exists in the parent; it was observed more often after SFT in this small sample. With thinking disabled, the parent scored 1/5; SFT had one correct and one incorrect graded attempt plus three verifier timeouts. Those missing grades prevent a complete accuracy comparison and are not counted as zero. This is a small diagnostic sample, not a full BixBench result. See the [primary Pi results and matched controls](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069563534).

The run used the September 21 Datakit parent, biology traces only, three epochs, peak LR 1e-4, 128k sequences, effective batch 16, and a final-only checkpoint. The dataset contains 5,120 reconstructed windows and 73,894,261 assistant target tokens per epoch from 1,319 attempts across 264 tasks, without reward/completion filtering or replay data. The [published-input audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6069710545) found no supervised tool tags inside open reasoning; the cause of the observed Pi behavior remains unresolved.

Terminus-2 and the synthetic tasks are **secondary diagnostics** of format adherence and transfer to other harnesses. Terminus scored parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5 on the same real questions; this is not the primary measure of the Pi-trained model. The [Terminus trace analysis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083049902) and [completed prompt ablation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083809697) investigate format sensitivity. The latter accepted 36/36 parent versus 0/36 SFT first responses under the Terminus schema; this remains a secondary format-transfer diagnostic. A Terminus-specific workaround would not establish a fix for Pi.

## Description

Use the existing [Skill2Env Harbor release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env) to collect GLM-5.3 demonstrations for Snowball. This issue owns task selection, rollout collection, SFT, and the before/after experiment. [#9630](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9630) owns Skill2Env Atlas intake; [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258) owns biology evaluation coverage and protocols.

Start with biology tasks, prioritizing biological data analysis relevant to BixBench. If the usable pool is too small, consider a separately recorded expansion to general scientific data analysis and statistics. Keep relay methods, where a teacher takes over from student-generated actions, for a later experiment.

### Candidate data

The October 5 metadata inspection covered all 7,496 tasks in release revision 2, version `1.0.1`, with content digest `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. The 268 candidates are a source-skill and description-based shortlist, not an exhaustive taxonomy or a validated training pool.

| Candidate category | Tasks | Source-skill identifiers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Genomics and single-cell analysis | 95 | 40 |
| Proteins and structure | 49 | 16 |
| Chemistry and drug discovery | 45 | 22 |
| Biomedical data and lab workflows | 79 | 28 |
| Total | 268 | 106 |

Examples include paired airway RNA-seq analysis with PyDESeq2, sparse CELLxGENE summaries, Scanpy PBMC QC and clustering, DepMap dependency analysis, and pysam BAM/VCF processing. Different skill identifiers can cover related workflows; 106 identifiers do not establish 106 independent task families. Many released tasks repair pipelines against offline fixtures. Their usefulness for BixBench remains a hypothesis.

Skill2Env's [source attribution table](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env/blob/507eab4d9952968de2be98f8729d3c66d487285a/SkillHub/skillhub_source_licenses.csv) includes K-Dense scientific skills and AlterLab academic skills. Preserve task-specific source and license records when selecting data or sharing traces. The selection rule below preserves this initial shortlist independently of temporary local files.

### Pilot sequence

1. Review candidate instructions, environments, and graders. Six initial tasks passed reference/no-op controls. The user authorized direct collection on the other 262 metadata-selected candidates; those tasks have not passed additional controls. Review grader validity when interpreting scores; it is not a selection gate for the unfiltered baseline. Record any grader defects; the existing Atlas assessment found a grader defect in a separate three-task sample.
2. Freeze the task manifest and evaluation split. Group related tasks and shared-data variants when defining development and held-out sets. BixBench-overlap checking is not a prerequisite for this collection, as decided on October 5; preserve task provenance.
3. Pin the Snowball starting checkpoint, tokenizer, training recipe, agent harness, and evaluation settings. Run a small end-to-end collection and formatting check before expanding collection. Record compute budgets before launching sandbox or training work.
4. Generate GLM-5.3 trajectories. The initial collection finished five attempts per task on the six control-checked tasks, for 30 attempted rollouts. The expanded collection targets five attempts for each of the other 262 tasks, for 1,310 new attempts. Preserve every attempt, raw conversations, tool outputs, exact model settings, task revisions, and the full native reward vector; keep incomplete and ungraded outcomes separate. Inspect component-score distributions, solution diversity, and token volume. The first SFT baseline uses all available solver traces without reward or completion filtering. Preserve interrupted prefixes and record conversion or recovery gaps without manufacturing missing content. Rewards are graded; do not reduce them to binary success or require all components to equal 1 by default. Native executable rewards do not reproduce the paper's additional rubric-scoring layer.
5. Prepare all available solver traces for the first SFT baseline; the earlier 200–500 selected-trace target is superseded. Report attempted, complete, graded, and selected traces; component-score distributions; unique tasks and task families; total tokens; and supervised assistant tokens. Size the first SFT run from those observations; the target is a planning budget, not a proven minimum. Prioritize coverage of distinct tasks when expanding collection. Additional attempts on one task do not increase task diversity.
6. Train with loss on assistant turns, preserving user and tool messages as context. Evaluate the final checkpoint against the unchanged Snowball parent on the fixed BixBench protocol using the same Pi harness and budgets. Decide on broader evaluations after reviewing BixBench. Keep infrastructure failures separate from incorrect answers.

Recent Snowball work motivates a bounded test: a [5,000-conversation GLM continuation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9719) regressed on several benchmarks, while [other agent SFT mixtures](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/8669f5b6f97e4e3bae72344a8fd51f4b) improved agent benchmarks. Neither establishes a BixBench benefit from this dataset.

### Agreed SFT settings

| Setting | Selected value |
| --- | --- |
| Parent | `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`; revision `b8c07f7df1df65525abbfdbcd1572318ba11c42f` and native tokenizer/template pinned |
| Data | All available GLM/Pi biology solver traces; no reward or completion filter; no general SFT or pretraining replay |
| Run count and peak LR | One run at `1e-4` |
| Duration | Three epochs |
| Training sequence length | 131,072 tokens; verify actual lengths with the parent tokenizer |
| Effective global batch | 16 sequences per optimizer update; accumulation as needed |
| Parameter updates | Full-parameter SFT; imported router biases frozen, router weights and other model weights trained |
| Optimizer | Fresh AdamH; beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95, epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0, gradient clipping 1.0 |
| Schedule | 3% warmup, then cosine decay from 1e-4 to 1e-5 over the run |
| Checkpoints | Final model save/export only; no intermediate or per-epoch checkpoints |
| Initial evaluation | Parent and final model on BixBench with identical Pi harness and budgets; broader evaluations deferred until that result |

The nominal batch is 2,097,152 token positions per update, matching 64 × 32,768 in [the teacher-only reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9582). Masking, padding, and sequence construction determine actual supervised tokens. Three epochs and peak LR 1e-4 follow that precedent; its reported evaluations use final checkpoints, and its intermediate checkpoint cadence is undocumented. The final-only saving decision avoids repeated serialization and storage of this model.

Use reconstructed conversations with each actual assistant output supervised once, carried context masked, and interrupted outputs left without invented termination markers. The finalized dataset has 5,120 windows at length 131,072, 320 steps per epoch, and 960 steps total. Target four CoreWeave nodes with eight H100s each. BixBench comparison uses `bixbench-cli-marin-corrections@3` (205 tasks), Pi, one attempt per task, 32,768 context / 8,192 output, and matched grading. The CPU training coordinator is submitted; GPU training remains gated on cache verification.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Unfiltered GLM-5.3 demonstrations of biological analysis improve Snowball's held-out BixBench accuracy under the same harness and execution budget. Measure paired BixBench changes and uncertainty, task coverage, tool-format failures, and response lengths. Broader evaluation is deferred until the BixBench result. Review trace completeness, native grades, and sequence handling before training; preserve negative results.

## Status

The expanded collection completed all 1,310 original task/repetition slots. The final audit proves exactly five attempts per task, with no missing or duplicate pairs. Native reward vectors exist for 1,285 attempts; 25 are ungraded. There are 946 final assistant `stop` markers, 248 output-limit endings, 49 final tool-use stops, eight final error stops, and 59 without an exported final assistant stop reason. Agent timeouts are an overlapping exception class: 86 attempts record one. No verifier-error diagnostic was recorded. Native Pi sessions and ATIF trajectories are present for 1,251 attempts.

Native score patterns across the graded attempts are 574 vectors with every component equal to 1, 381 with mixed or partial component credit, and 330 with every component equal to 0. These remain graded vectors, not binary success labels. The 946 final `stop` markers cover 238 tasks; nine also record runner exceptions, so this marker alone does not establish a clean run. A historical structural screen requiring native session and trajectory, no exception or recorded verifier error, and matched tool calls/replies retains 933 normal candidates. Of those, 558 have every component equal to 1 and cover 161 tasks. Their provider-counted output usage totals 24,112,468 tokens; this includes reasoning and possible auxiliary compaction output and is not a unique Snowball-supervised token count. Four normal traces have unresolved tool-call diagnostics. These screening counts are diagnostic subsets and do not define the unfiltered training pool.

The original batch retained 875 attempts: 829 verified per-attempt archives and 46 [verified fallback recoveries](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6016912375). The continuation executed only the remaining 435 slots and verified all 435 checkpoints, with no further checkpoint failures. It completed at 14:46:11 UTC; cleanup at 14:46:14 reported zero owned sandboxes. The small final Iris archive and completion audit were copied to private durable storage and retrieved for SHA-256 verification. Final archive SHA-256: `4b06bdb9e491145acaddddb0cd44928191386b22b80b3061a3b1a18c5511e68a` (2,240,445 bytes). Original native grades, checkpoint-failure labels, and interrupted-stream diagnostics are preserved.

Both cohorts used native Pi 0.87.0 with 131,072 total context, 32,768 solver output, thinking enabled, native compaction, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, repetition seeds 0–4, and up to 64 concurrent workers. The continuation repaired capture closure and retried a startup that was preempted before teacher generation; it did not rerun attempted slots. Original expanded protocol SHA-256: `24ebb14feb54c3ec97f4c79732a7d42efb2c8cc7c792c2bc6e714dbeb6833997`; continuation: `36e7a611fb25f8e6625934b123ad00f6b33cdace57945b32d7ac5a7ef9852a58`; 262-task manifest: `87f0276f2fe2a3675eb875079363d20d321a80ca216e265539c39a6524f7cd75`. Source archives, notices, launch snapshots, native results, and raw captures are retained.

The six-task control batch is complete: all reference reward components were 1.0 and all no-op components were 0.0, with verifier diagnostics reviewed. The other candidates remain a metadata shortlist. The [seven-attempt Terminus-2 batch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6004311716) is retained separately as diagnostic evidence; its continuation is superseded.

Pi collection completed all 30 planned attempts and retained 29 native reward vectors. Endings: 17 normal, eight output-limited, four agent timeouts, and one ungraded `DaytonaBadGatewayError`. No verifier errors were recorded. The 17 normal traces have matched tool calls and replies, with full or partial native component credit. They cover DepMap, pysam, CELLxGENE, PyDESeq2, and Scanpy; all five scikit-bio attempts ended at an output limit. They contain 869,472 provider-counted output tokens before reward selection and target-tokenizer accounting. No filtering has been applied; the first baseline retains all available solver traces.

Native Pi sessions and ATIF trajectories were retained for 26/30 attempts. Three timeouts lost native log export because `pi.txt` changed during archiving; the infrastructure failure also lacks native agent logs. Raw API captures are retained for all 30 attempts, including three interrupted response streams. The four timeout traces contain repeated identical tool exchanges. The complete archive, source notices, per-file hashes, configuration, launcher, and audit are privately preserved. Archive SHA-256: `61671f943850c0601a9febb3058bf3e1e2df3689b7ef06594280aa89ce087c9f`. No Daytona sandboxes remain.

The teacher uses native Pi 0.87.0, matching the runtime pin in [evaluation policy #9409](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9409), with the [Skill2Env paper, section 3.4](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env/blob/main/paper/Skill2Env_arXiv.pdf) teacher budget: 131,072 total context tokens, a 32,768-token solver output cap, high thinking, and native compaction. Pi's high setting maps to GLM chat-template thinking enabled; no provider `reasoning_effort` tier is sent. BixBench policy instead uses 32,768 total context and 8,192 output tokens; collection and evaluation budgets remain separate. Live requests obeyed the configured cap, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, and repetition seeds 0–4. The largest observed prompt was 98,346 tokens; compaction used a 16,384-token output cap. This is not a full context-boundary stress test.

Execution uses upstream Harbor `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3` with a configuration-only adapter around Pi. Native tools, prompt, loop, task resources, and component grades are retained. Setup allows the recorded package mirrors; agent execution allows the scoped model endpoint, and verification retains the task's no-network policy. The initial six-task collection used at most three concurrent trials, native 30-minute agent timeouts, a six-hour batch limit, and no whole-trial retries. The expanded batch retains native timeouts and task resources, with the concurrency and batch limit recorded above. Frozen protocol SHA-256: `33a9e03a0a426b9d1ed8c328f2743ec4efa9b0fdf4425907d4f93dce156aa338`. BixBench-overlap checking is not a prerequisite.

Before SFT, recover available recorded content, validate native-format conversion and loss masks, and count supervised tokens. Keep output limits, repeated tool loops, missing exports, and grader diagnostics as annotations. Pin the selected parent weights and tokenizer, validate the chosen training recipe and long-conversation handling, and freeze the BixBench evaluation protocol. No training or BixBench comparison has run.

## Links

- [Completed Pi collection and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6006473943).
- Logbook: dated updates in this issue; keep this body current as decisions change.
- W&B report: pending the first training run.
- Dataset assessment and known grader issue: [#9630](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9630).
- Biology evaluation protocols and baselines: [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258).
- Source project: [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env).

## Decision Log

- 2026-10-05: Start with released Skill2Env biology tasks and complete GLM-only demonstrations. Use native component rewards to select traces and assistant-only SFT. Defer relay methods.
- 2026-10-05: Treat general scientific data analysis as a possible expansion if the validated biology pool is insufficient.
- 2026-10-05: Track this experiment here and link its evaluation results from #9258. Preserve Atlas intake under #9630.
- 2026-10-05: Completed reference/no-op controls on six pinned tasks. Collection: five attempts per task, 30 total. Treat rewards as graded vectors and choose the SFT selection policy after inspecting pilot distributions; this supersedes earlier binary verified-success wording.

- 2026-10-05: Authorized the 30-rollout collection and removed BixBench-overlap checking as a prerequisite. Preserve source provenance and full component rewards.
- 2026-10-05: Superseded Terminus-2 with Pi to match the intended Snowball harness. Selected the paper's 128k context / 32k output teacher budget if supported. Retain the seven prior attempts separately; do not resume their queue.

- 2026-10-06: Completed the 30-attempt Pi batch with 29 native reward vectors and 17 normal trace candidates. Preserve all native scores and raw captures; keep output-limit endings, timeouts, and the ungraded infrastructure failure separate. SFT selection and training remain pending.

- 2026-10-06: Authorized five attempts for every remaining shortlisted biology task (262 tasks; 1,310 new attempts) while unattended. Selected 64 concurrent rollouts after checking bulk inference guidance and sandbox quota. Preserve every native reward vector and verified private artifacts; defer SFT selection and training.

- 2026-10-06: Recovered the first expanded job's 46 fallback attempts without changing native grades. Continue only the 435 unattempted slots; replace the short capture-close window with a bounded 35-minute wait outside the upload lock. Preserve all prior attempts, including incomplete and ungraded outcomes.

- 2026-10-06: Completed all 1,310 expanded slots without duplicates; all evidence is retained and continuation sandbox cleanup is complete. Keep the issue open for the planned SFT and evaluation stages.

- 2026-10-06: Selected an unfiltered first SFT baseline using all available GLM/Pi solver traces, including truncated and interrupted prefixes; supersedes earlier reward and completeness selection proposals. Preserve scores as annotations and avoid artificial termination targets. GitHub and Discord precedents support a bounded continuation but leave parent, mixture, and hyperparameters open.

- 2026-10-06: Selected September 21 Datakit SFT, biology traces only with no replay, one run at peak LR 1e-4, three epochs, 131,072-token training sequences, and effective global batch 16. Save/export and evaluate the final model only; per-epoch checkpointing was dropped because of model-size overhead.

- 2026-10-06: Confirmed full-parameter SFT with fresh AdamH (betas 0.9/0.95, epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0, clip 1.0), 3% warmup, cosine decay from 1e-4 to 1e-5, and frozen imported router biases. Start evaluation with BixBench alone; decide on other evaluations after its result.

- 2026-10-06: Selected reconstructed conversations and CoreWeave H100 compute (32 GPUs). Finalized 5,120 windows with 73,894,261 supervised tokens per epoch; batch 16 and three epochs give 960 steps. All 58 preparation artifacts passed full SHA-256 readback. Preserve every available solver output, crop only masked context where necessary, and finish trainer validation before launch.

## Conclusion

Collection and the agreed three-epoch, biology-only SFT run are complete. Pi is the primary evaluation harness because it matches teacher collection and intended deployment. The current Pi/BixBench diagnostic does not establish an SFT improvement: thinking-enabled accuracy was parent 1/5 versus SFT 0/5, and thinking-disabled SFT has only two graded attempts out of five. An unexecuted tool call in the final parsed reasoning field was observed in one of five thinking-enabled parent traces and all five SFT traces. It is a pre-existing failure pattern that appeared more frequently after SFT in this sample; it is not unique to the SFT checkpoint. The small sample and incomplete grading limit any broader accuracy claim.

This experiment is finished at the owner's request. The unresolved cause of the Pi formatting behavior and the three missing thinking-disabled SFT grades are accepted limitations of the final result, not outstanding work under this issue. No further runs or debugging are planned here. Any future experiment would have a separate scope and should use Pi as its primary evaluation harness.

Terminus-2 and synthetic tasks remain secondary diagnostics. The [completed prompt ablation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9775#issuecomment-6083809697) accepted 36/36 parent versus 0/36 SFT first responses under the Terminus schema. These findings do not establish a remedy for the primary Pi failures. Results and analysis are preserved, and the final diagnostic inference servers have stopped.

topics.title: [iris] Cached job env reaches child jobs after the job scrubs its secrets
topics.body:
Iris caches a job's environment before the job's own code runs, so a job that scrubs secrets from `os.environ` and `IRIS_JOB_ENV` at startup still hands the unscrubbed environment to any non-sandbox child job it launches.

Observed on `cw-us-east-02a` during a Zephyr feasibility spike for Taskforge: the Taskforge queue job removes `GLM_API_TOKEN`, `WANDB_API_KEY` and the other host secrets from its environment at start (`scrub_child_environment`), and afterwards both `os.environ` and `IRIS_JOB_ENV` are clean. The job environment Iris had already cached still held `GLM_API_TOKEN` and `WANDB_API_KEY`, so a non-sandbox child job would inherit them. Sandbox children (ShellSim, bwrap, gVisor) received no env in this run; gVisor sandboxes did see the `IRIS_*` variables and the Kubernetes service addresses, including the controller's.

Asks: (1) a documented way for a job to launch children with an explicit environment that does not include the parent's cached env (an allowlist on the child job spec, or a per-submission `inherit_env=False`); (2) sandbox pods should not receive `IRIS_*` variables or the controller's service address unless the submitter asks for them, since model-controlled code runs there.

Related earlier notes on the Taskforge side: CoreWeave `task_env` injecting object-store keys into pods (not reproduced on `cw-rno2a` in this spike) and child jobs inheriting a parent's explicit `-e` secrets.

topics.title: Complete and validate online multi-harness RL integration
topics.body:
Complete the integration and end-to-end validation of online multi-harness RL in MarinSkyRL through Marin's BFCL entrypoint. The campaign demonstrated multi-harness collection and native offline DPO, but did not verify a complete online RL optimizer update. Most underlying components exist; this task should connect and validate them rather than introduce a parallel training stack.

The [public readiness inventory](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/technical-progress-20261011.md) identifies the concrete gap: the older online launcher has four harness profiles and an RL recipe, but disables inline evaluation and resolves an older recovery export. The native DPO path has the demonstrated Pi evaluation and checkpoint/export wiring. [Pinned Marin entrypoints](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl), [MarinSkyRL runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/fa6da4d8c67ed17b3fa69f689d9b444694683f8a), [Harbor runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/436d0c92ed2fbb679438cd750e5fab3328153c31).

Done when:

- Wire an explicitly pinned initializer, current Daytona backend/snapshot handling, live policy inference, harness assignment, native trace/token/logprob capture, reward/advantage construction, optimizer updates, inference synchronization, and recurring evaluation into one maintained entrypoint.
- Make harness assignment and mixture weights explicit. Existing task-index routing does not establish randomized same-task cross-harness coverage. Preserve native tool interfaces and exact model-visible history, including multi-turn compaction and generation masks.
- Demonstrate single-harness smokes for Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, and Mini-SWE, then a mixed-harness smoke. Require actual non-skipped optimizer updates and subsequent rollouts from updated weights, finite training metrics, correct policy-version provenance, save/resume, and an independently loadable export. Successful job exit alone is insufficient.
- Verify reward/error taxonomy: infrastructure failures are not silently treated as policy failures, and policy-scoreable errors retain verifier outcomes. Exercise timeouts, missing tool results, and partial completed batches without discarding valid immutable work.
- Connect baseline, periodic, and terminal Pi validation using the demonstrated native evaluation path; run separate full panels across harnesses for cross-harness assessment. A single inline harness does not establish multi-harness robustness.
- Run a bounded online learning experiment on complement-only tasks, with no BFCL-Parity training leakage. Publish exact pins, placement, hyperparameters, update/rollout receipts, costs, and policy-matched results. Separately report integration completion and whether task performance improves.
- Record the original campaign's unresolved scientific target: substantial BFCL-Parity improvement with the worst harness at least 70% of the best. Failure to achieve that target must not erase a verified integration result, nor should an integration pass be called learning success.

The [native DPO smoke](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/final-pipeline-v356-verified.json) provides a reuse target, not evidence that online RL is complete. [Distributed numerical-equivalence experiments](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/969) remain a separate verification follow-up, not three established defects or a prerequisite for this integration task. [Campaign closeout #10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040); related work: [localized online feedback #10043](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043) and [datakit local-pair mining #10042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10042).

topics.title: [grug] Route QBRoutedMoE through the jax_triton top-k kernel
topics.body:
QBRoutedMoE now selects experts with `levanter.grug._moe.topk.top_k_indices`, called per token shard inside `shard_map`, in place of `jax.lax.top_k`. That is the jax_triton kernel from #9830, which the hero model already uses. `jax.lax.top_k` still handles rows of 1,024 or more (XLA:GPU runs its own top-k kernel on those), non-float32 inputs, non-GPU backends and environments without jax-triton.

On AMD, jax-triton 0.3.1 with triton 3.6.0, Levanter's GPU pins, compiles the kernel for ROCm with jaxlib 0.11.1 or newer. jaxlib 0.11.0 never loads `jax_rocm10_plugin`'s Triton launcher, so there the kernel falls back to `jax.lax.top_k`.

Time per call in ms, from 16 calls on distinct inputs in one executable, median of 5 runs. The shapes are the router logits per call of the hero model and of the June Snowball model:

| shape, k | GPU | `lax.top_k` | jax_triton (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [65536, 384], 9 (hero) | GB200 | 0.837 | 0.0754 |
| [65536, 384], 9 (hero) | H100 | 1.107 | 0.0954 |
| [65536, 384], 9 (hero) | MI300X | 0.847 | 0.0665 |
| [65536, 384], 9 (hero) | MI350X | 1.000 | 0.0570 |
| [32768, 256], 5 (June) | GB200 | 0.229 | 0.0207 |
| [32768, 256], 5 (June) | H100 | 0.308 | 0.0238 |
| [32768, 256], 5 (June) | MI300X | 0.351 | 0.0246 |
| [32768, 256], 5 (June) | MI350X | 0.402 | 0.0167 |

The AMD rows ran on jax 0.11.1, jax_rocm10_plugin 0.11.1+rocm10.1.0, jax-triton 0.3.1 and triton 3.6.0, with the AMD HPC Fund cluster's ROCm 7.2 libraries on the library path, as `experiments/amd/hpcfund/run_gpu.sh` leaves them. The `lax.top_k` baseline depends on that: with only the wheel's own ROCm libraries loaded, `lax.top_k` on MI350X takes 2.4 ms (hero) and 1.7 ms (June), while the kernel times do not change. The kernel code is unchanged since #9830; the NVIDIA rows are earlier measurements of it with the same harness.

On NVIDIA, the models that use QBRoutedMoE (`experiments/grug/moe`, `experiments/grug/moe_hero_fsdp` and `experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe`) now run the kernel, because Levanter's GPU extra installs jax-triton. In the optimized HLO of the June training step on H100 and GB200, the 4 `sort` ops of main's routing become 2 `triton_kernel_call`s, and the all-gathers, all-reduces and reduce-scatters are unchanged. Step time does not change measurably. June model at full width with 4 layers and sequence length 4096, ring expert parallelism over the node, `xla_flash` attention and XLA `ragged_dot`; median of steps 2-19 per run, runs alternating between main and this PR:

| GPU | Tokens per GPU | Runs per side | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4x GB200 | 8,192 | 4 | 0.5742 s (0.5723-0.5759) | 0.5740 s (0.5719-0.5760) |
| 8x H100 | 16,384 | 5 | 1.457 s (1.403-1.508) | 1.513 s (1.336-1.539) |

On H100, step time varied between runs of the same code: main's five runs spanned 1.403-1.508 s (7%) and this PR's 1.336-1.539 s (15%). Five runs per side cannot separate the two. Scaled to these shapes, the per-call times above put the saving below 0.1% of a step. At 16,384 tokens per GPU on GB200, runs of both variants intermittently hung in a training step or ran out of memory, so those runs are left out. TPU step time was not measured; there `top_k_indices` falls back to `lax.top_k` inside the same `shard_map`.

On MI300X and MI350X the kernel's indices equal those of `lax.top_k` computed on the CPU, for widths 37 to 1,023 and k up to 37, on random, tied, constant, ±0, ±inf and NaN rows. ROCm's own `lax.top_k` ties -0 with +0 and orders NaN payloads differently, while the kernel follows XLA:CPU and CUDA. The GPU tests therefore check the kernel's output against `lax.top_k` run on the CPU backend.

The AMD venv recipe in `experiments/amd/hpcfund/README.md` still installs jaxlib 0.11.0 without jax-triton, so runs from it silently keep `lax.top_k` until that recipe moves to 0.11.1.

Supersedes #9889, which added a separate ROCm-only Pallas kernel for power-of-two widths.

topics.title: [grug] Keep AdamH updates finite on zero-norm matrices
topics.body:
scale_by_adamh projects onto the parameter's Frobenius sphere by dividing by
the updated matrix norm. A zero matrix stays zero through a zero learning-rate
or zero-gradient step, so the division is 0/0 and the update is NaN. Floor
that norm at 1e-10, the same floor the direction step already uses.

Fixes #9054

topics.title: [fast-track] Marin Belay v1: hill-climb the scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss, 8 min on 8×H100)
topics.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. The baseline's settings were tuned for the baseline, not for the new idea. ## Architecture (current best, d512) The diagrams below show **clean KMA**. The current best recipe adds the components listed under **Status → Current best recipe**: MLA key norm and key offset, a gated bigram-memory AttnRes source, ReLU² experts, and optimizer, schedule and logit changes. The diagrams show d512; the other rungs differ in the Shape table only. **1. Layer stack and Block Attention Residuals.** Every sublayer reads its input through its own AttnRes gate, a per-token softmax over the residual history. At d512 each layer closes an AttnRes block, so the history at layer *i* is the embedding plus one sum per earlier layer. [¹](#arch-note) ```mermaid flowchart TB tok["token ids
B × 4096, packed documents"] --> emb["token embedding
16384 × 512"] emb --> en["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] en --> S0(["source 0
embedding"]) S0 --> L0 subgraph STACK["6 layers: local KDA ×4, global MLA ×2 (every 4th + last)"] direction TB L0["layer 0 · KDA + MoE"] --> L1["layer 1 · KDA + MoE"] --> L2["layer 2 · KDA + MoE"] L2 --> L3["layer 3 · MLA + Inkling + MoE"] --> L4["layer 4 · KDA + MoE"] --> L5["layer 5 · MLA + Inkling + MoE"] end L0 -. "block sum b0" .-> H L1 -. "b1" .-> H L2 -. "b2" .-> H L3 -. "b3" .-> H L4 -. "b4" .-> H S0 -.-> H H[("AttnRes history, read by every gate
[embedding, b0 … b(i−1)]
+ running partial")] L5 --> FG["final AttnRes gate
softmax over embedding, b0…b4, partial"] FG --> fn["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] fn --> head["lm_head (untied) 512 × 16384
fused CE, vocab tile 8192, z-loss 1e-4"] head --> loss(["next-token loss"]) ``` **2. One layer.** The two sublayers each have an AttnRes gate. The MoE gate also sees the attention output written just before it, as the running partial. ```mermaid flowchart TB Hin[("history
embedding + b0…b(i−1)")] --> GA subgraph GATE["AttnRes gate (one per sublayer, 13 at d512)"] direction TB GA["logit_n = q · rms_norm(source_n)
q ∈ ℝ⁵¹², zero-init (uniform mix)
frozen key norm"] --> SM["softmax over sources
weighted sum of raw sources"] end SM --> A1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MIX{{"mixer
KDA (local) or MLA + Inkling (global)"}} MIX --> SCA["ShortConv (MLA layers only)"] --> PA(["partial = attn out"]) PA --> GM["AttnRes gate
history + partial"] Hin --> GM GM --> M1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MOE{{"LatentMoE + 2 shared experts"}} MOE --> SCM["ShortConv"] --> PB(["block b_i = attn out + MoE out"]) PB --> Hout[("appended to history")] ``` **3a. Kimi Delta Attention, the local mixer (layers 0, 1, 2, 4 at d512; D = 512, 4 heads × 128).** ```mermaid flowchart TB kx["x"] --> kq["q = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_q))"] & kk["k = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_k))"] & kv["v = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_v))"] kx --> kg["decay g = −5 · σ(exp(A_log) · (x W_a↓ W_a↑ + dt_bias))
rank-128 gate, per channel; A_log per head"] kx --> kb["write strength β = σ(x W_β), per head"] kq & kk --> kn["L2-norm q, k; q × 1/√128"] kn & kv & kg & kb --> rec["delta rule, chunked Pallas kernels (chunk 16)
S_t = (I − β k kᵀ) Diag(e^g) S_{t−1} + β k vᵀ
o_t = S_tᵀ q_t · state resets at document starts"] rec --> kon["per-head RMSNorm (shared 128-wide scale)"] --> kog["× σ(x W_g), per channel"] --> ko["W_o → sublayer out
no RoPE, no window, no output ShortConv"] ``` **3b. MLA + Inkling, the global mixer (layers 3 and 5 at d512).** ```mermaid flowchart TB mx["x"] --> mq["q = x W_q (full rank, 4 × 128)"] mx --> ml["KV latent = RMSNorm(x W_dkv), 512 wide, learnable gain"] --> mk["k = latent W_uk"] & mv["v = latent W_uv"] mx --> rel["Inkling bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]
R = x W_r (16 per head) · P 16 × 1024, shared across heads"] mq & mk & mv & rel --> fa["FA4 causal attention (fwd + SM90 bwd)
logits × 1/√128 (qk_mult 1) · no RoPE · no QK-norm
Inkling bias added before softmax"] fa --> xsa["XSA: subtract each head's component along its own v"] --> mg["× 2σ(x W_gate), per head, zero-init"] --> mo["W_o → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` **3c. LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing (every layer).** ```mermaid flowchart TB ex["x (512)"] --> fused["one fused GEMM:
router · W_latent↓ · shared-expert gate/up"] fused --> rt["router logits (fp32)
top-(8+1) on logit − β_QB; 9th = threshold α"] rt --> qb["QB: β_e = global (1 − 8/384) quantile of logit − α
10k-bin histogram each step; router bias = −β, not trained"] rt --> cw["combine weights = σ(unbiased logits) of the top 8,
renormalized to sum to 2.5"] fused --> lat["latent = RMSNorm(x W_latent↓), 256 wide"] lat & cw --> ep["384 SwiGLU experts, hidden 256
pooled-wave EP all-to-all over 8 GPUs, capacity 1.15"] ep --> up["W_latent↑ 256 → 512"] fused --> sh["2 shared SwiGLU experts, 512 → 256 → 512
down projections fused into one GEMM"] up & sh --> sum["routed + shared → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` ¹ AttnRes rolls a new block at layer *i* while `i % max(1, L // 8) == 0` and fewer than 8 blocks exist. At d512 and d768 every layer closes a block. At d1024 (12 layers) and d1280 (14 layers) only layers 0–7 do, so layers 8 and up all accumulate into one running partial instead of their own blocks. **Optimizer routing:** - **MuonH:** every attention and MoE matrix, and every GatedNorm (KDA `W_β` at 2× the MuonH LR). - **AdamH:** lm_head. - **Adam:** embedding, router, attention output gate, norm gains, ShortConv kernels, KDA decay parameters, Inkling weights. - **Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR:** the AttnRes queries. ## Baseline: clean KMA Branch [`fasttrack-moe-kma`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/fasttrack-moe-kma) @ `4eba59cafa`. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. Only the router and the attention output gate get decoupled weight decay (0.02). No other parameter gets weight decay, and there's no gradient clipping. - **Schedule:** 1% warmup, then linear decay to 0.05× peak. - **Peak values** from `MoeHeuristic` (they depend on tokens, width and batch): - Adam LR = `0.0876 · tokens^−0.346 · D^−0.345 · √(tokens per batch)`. - MuonH LR = 13/3 × Adam LR. - β2 = `0.999^(tokens per batch / 131072)`. - ε = `9.68e−18 · √(steps)`. - At d512 with 2384 steps: MuonH LR 0.0227, Adam LR 0.0052, β2 0.996, ε 4.7e−16. Submit at **batch** priority (the launcher's default is interactive, so pass it): ``` NO_PROXY="*" uv run python -m experiments.grug.fast_track.launch --submit \ --target-cluster cw-us-east-02a --priority batch \ --run-id --size d512 --recipe kma --num-steps <8-min steps> --version ``` ## Compute - cw-us-east-02a at **batch** priority. - **At most 10 active runs at once**, probes included. - **Limit runs above d768** to keep the experimentation rate high. d1024 and d1280 runs take hours and hold a slot the whole time, so save them for changes that have already passed gate 1 or that need extra scales because of curve-fitting risk. - Don't save checkpoints (the launcher default). ## For humans Comment with a research direction for the agent, for example "try X", or "combine A and B". The agent picks up new comments at its next batch. The main goal of a single experiment should be to learn about the system. This means that if you tweak one knob and the loss goes off the rails, the experiment can still be considered a success! We better understand the system sensitivity! Building knowledge through failed experiments will bring us closer to the long term goal of better models. ## For the agent - Read `experiments/grug/fast_track/README.md` and `agent.md` first. Where they differ from this issue, this issue wins; the main difference is the fixed-time objective. - Run 5–10 experiments per batch, and prioritize human comments when picking the next one. - Ask for clarification in the thread if helpful, but never hold a batch waiting for an answer: state your assumption and correct it in the next batch. - Start at d512. When a change beats the current best by more than 0.005, validate it at d768. - Post **one comment per batch** and edit it as runs finish. Start it with 🤖 and include: - the batch goal, and which human comments it addresses; - a table with one row per run: change | branch@commit | W&B link | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ vs current best; - a 1–3 line takeaway and the planned next batch. - **Branches:** prefix with `ladderclimb_v1_`, and link the exact commit each job ran. - **W&B:** project `marin_moe`, with short prefixed run IDs such as `lc1-b03-…` (names over 128 characters fail at init). - Add the `agent-generated` label to any issue or PR you open. - Keep the **Status** table below updated with a concise chronology of improvements. ## Studies Deep dives and multi-batch studies, newest first. Pages are claude.ai artifacts; batch comments hold the plan, every run and the numbers. | study | what it found | page | batch comments | |---|---|---|---| | **Hyperball decay per matrix** | The MuonH/AdamH hyperball re-projection acts as a per-matrix weight decay that depends on the update's direction (`decay = 1 − |W|/|W+u|` ≈ `lr·cos(W,u) + lr²/2`). Logged every step for every matrix on the ragged base (`lc1-b191-hb2`, 2.9631). Typical matrices decay 0.06–0.10%/step mid-run with cos ≈ 0.07–0.10, so over 90% of the decay comes from updates leaning outward, not from the orthogonal part. Odd ones: KDA `w_beta` (all 4 layers) decays 2–3× anything else (0.17–0.26%/step, 1.3% early) with 4× the rescale and inward swings; the AdamH lm head has the lowest median (0.045%) but the largest spikes (p99 1.27%, cos up to 0.66); layer-5 MLA `w_o` spikes too (p99 1.0%); layer-5 MLA `w_uv` is the only large projection with inward steps; gated-norm matrices hold the highest sustained decay, rising with depth. Code: `--opt-set log_hyperball_decay=true` (`hyperball_metrics`). | [Hyperball Decay Atlas](https://claude.ai/artifact/74PcjNW2PaNkYV5btbq3Ug) | — | | **Learned RMSNorm gains** | What every learned RMSNorm gain learns on candidate 11 (linear gains), per module. No gain goes negative; gains span about 700× across modules (`embed2_norm` 0.01–0.45, `final_norm` up to 7.6) but cluster tightly within one, and the largest (`final_norm`, MoE latent norms) are still rising at the end. Gain functions: `e^w` −0.0026 (within noise; `final_norm` climbs to 15), softplus −0.0008, `2·sigmoid` +0.115 (pins `final_norm` at its cap of 2). Learned output scalars on every sublayer are neutral (linear −0.0003, `2·sigmoid` −0.0015). Code: `norm_gain_fn`, `sublayer_scale_fn`, `norm_gain_lr_mult`, `--weight-diagnostics`. | [Learned RMSNorm Gains](https://claude.ai/artifact/KcoMDyEcULNMFebyS5eTRQ) | [181](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5985074958) | | **lm_head soft-cap shape** | Tanh caps 10–12 are flat on the current recipe (11: +0.0004 on 2 seeds). `A·σ((z+B)/C)` is a tanh cap `A/2` on `A/(4C)·(z+B)`, so its knobs are cap, gain and shift. At cap 11, shift ±4 and gain 0.8 / 1.25 all land within the 0.003 same-function noise; lower gain and either shift lean worse. Kept tanh 10. | — | [batch 32](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5852265563), [43](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5853836517), [175](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5945519263) | | **Learning a fact from one exposure** | Candidate 10 (d512, seed 0) re-scored the exact training batches of steps 1000 and 2200 at every step around their exposure, against the other, not-yet-seen batch as control. The seen batch keeps improving after the update: −0.49 nats/token peak 15 steps later at step 1000, −0.24 peak about 50 steps later at step 2200 (momentum; the slow AdEMAMix buffer has about a 50-step memory). The early gain is mostly forgotten by step 2200 (≈ −0.01); the late one mostly stays (−0.19 at the end, EMA too). topics.title: [experiment] BFCL multi-harness DPO recovery: results and remaining work
topics.body:
## TL;DR

The BFCL multi-harness recovery campaign did not reach its goal. We exercised DPO (direct preference optimization) in Levanter, implemented and tested native DPO in MarinSkyRL, and built trace retention, preference curation, and multi-harness collection infrastructure. The extended native DPO run degraded Pi accuracy from 34/123 at initialization to 10/123 after four updates and 0/123 after eight; we stopped it after preserving intermediate evaluations. Harness transfer was partial and large score differences persisted across harnesses. A separate model-merging campaign recovered substantially more measured BFCL-Parity performance than the DPO recipes tested here, with important selection and comparability limits.

## Description

The original objective was to improve function calling from the Grug-67B-A2B Antidoom/RLVR1 step-12 lineage and demonstrate multi-harness robustness: the worst harness should reach at least 70% of the best harness's score. Grug is a mixture-of-experts model with approximately 67 billion total and 2 billion active parameters; Antidoom/RLVR1 identifies its prior de-looping and reinforcement-learning checkpoint lineage. Labels such as `.304` and `.356` are campaign run/artifact identifiers. Training used the 3,518-task BFCL complement, excluding the 123 BFCL-Parity tasks. Offline DPO was used to improve the weak starting policy before attempting further online RL.

BFCL-Parity is Harbor's `bfcl_parity@1.0` adaptation of the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard. Pi, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Mini-SWE are agent harnesses that provide prompts, tool interfaces, and execution loops around the model. Each evaluation task receives one agent trial; accuracy means passing the task verifier. These tasks require `/app/result.json`, whose existence alone is insufficient for success. The scores below are adaptation-specific solve rates, not standard BFCL leaderboard scores. See the [public evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9566).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Learn function-calling behavior that transfers across harnesses while preserving task accuracy. The campaign tested whole-trajectory preference training, not the localized token/action objectives proposed in the follow-ups.

## Status

Learning work is stopped. The campaign achieved these infrastructure milestones:

- Levanter DPO produced the `.304` initializer after two additional optimizer updates and a 39-shard HF-format export. This checkpoint descended from an earlier 58-update DPO warm start; it was not trained directly from the original model in two updates. [Export receipt](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/daytona-expanded-training-v304-verified.json).
- Native DPO was [merged into MarinSkyRL in #954](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/954). Pipeline smoke `.356` connected fresh collection, curation, four applied updates, Pi evaluation, and export. Its 64-pair batch contained one newly collected pair; this was not an all-harness fresh-data smoke. Accuracy fell from 28/123 to 7/123. [Optimizer and pipeline receipt](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/final-pipeline-v356-verified.json).
- The collection/curation path retains teacher/student traces, exact tokens and masks where captured, verifier outcomes, task identities, immutable partial batches, and preference provenance. Four harnesses supplied the final training cohort; Pi was the evaluation harness. These components support future datakit mining, but do not yet implement verified same-history local repair pairs. [Infrastructure inventory](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/technical-progress-20261011.md), [pinned campaign code](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/experiments/post_training/bfcl_rl).
- A complete online multi-harness RL optimizer loop was not demonstrated. Collection, native trace capture, rollout configuration, and training components exist; their full on-policy integration remains unverified. Some fixes remain on campaign branches or open PRs.

The final native DPO input contained 1,712 pairs from 633 tasks unseen by the initializer's recorded training lineage. We planned 107 updates at 16 pairs/update, with Pi validation before training and every four updates. Applied updates are verified through 35, with nine completed evaluation panels and a partial update-36 panel. The initializer remained the best evaluated checkpoint. [Collapse analysis](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/dpo-collapse-investigation-20261011.md), [archive/stop receipt](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/12096f05afc65fa3ec29e60e240d5efac624cb6b/trials/final-dpo-forensics-stop-verified.json).

## Results and limits

Levanter's short `.304` continuation improved the measured panel relative to its `.26` warm start: Pi 23/122 to 35/123, Claude Code 15/123 to 29/123, OpenCode 8/123 to 24/123, and Mini-SWE 8/123 to 16/123. The Pi baseline attempted 123 tasks with one infrastructure-ungraded result. These are single panel comparisons, not repeated statistical estimates. Public warm-start receipts: [Pi](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-pi-verified.json), [Claude Code](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-claude-code-verified.json), [OpenCode](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-opencode-verified.json), [Mini-SWE](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/blob/7c63db4501ba6d3a523db18726d3855cf96b0afb/trials/daytona-reference-parity-v311-2026.10.04.26-mini-swe-agent-verified.json).

The earlier `.304` panel scored Pi 35/123 (28.46%), Claude Code 29/123 (23.58%), OpenCode 24/123 (19.51%), and Mini-SWE 16/123 (13.01%). Codex covered only 105/123 tasks and was not a valid canonical panel. The worst valid score was 46% of the best, below the required 70%. These results show harness-dependent performance; they do not isolate a causal training-mixture effect. The later 34/123 native-run baseline is a separate evaluation of the initializer.

The best related published merge, [Shared100](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-NUPA-BFCL-Shared100-2026.10.09/tree/462ad9af071055da39ef4bfea1d4ba2c9429a223), scored 60/123 (48.78%) on BFCL-Parity Pi, versus `.304`'s 35/123. In our experiments, merging recovered more measured performance than the tested DPO recipes. However, BFCL-Parity activation traces informed expert selection in the merge campaign, and the benchmark was reused for model selection. Its score is an optimization result, not a clean held-out or controlled causal comparison with DPO. Parent mixtures and training histories differ, and the merge's Pi score does not establish multi-harness robustness. [Merge campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9975).

At native DPO update 8, all 123 tasks lacked the required result file. Successful file-writing demonstrations existed in the preference data. Rejected responses contributed about 7.24 times as many supervised tokens as chosen responses, with extreme tool-syntax repetition. These observations motivate local, bounded training targets. They do not establish the precise gradient mechanism behind the collapse. Independent distributed-update and training-to-serving numerical equivalence remain [deferred verification experiments](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/969), not discovered bugs.

## Links

Datakit is [Marin's data preparation and chat-rendering library](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/04eb02163c432435987ac875b9c9907da7ab8211/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit). Linked historical reports retain local/internal provenance paths; the public release supports aggregate inspection rather than complete independent replay. Evaluation runtime pins also differ between the DPO and merge campaigns, so their results are separate campaign measurements.

- [Public screened campaign artifacts](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026.10.11/tree/9be5d36578c27140a75caac1e31ecdefb76cff0b): 7,356 files, reports, scripts, configurations, aggregate receipts, model publication verification, and an exclusion manifest. Raw conversations, private DPO datasets, third-party payloads, secrets, and runtime directories are withheld. Public aggregates do not permit independent replay of every private-trace analysis.
- [Best DPO initializer, BFCL-Recovery (`.304`)](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-BFCL-Recovery/tree/850a32627724d274004241dd10f6cb46fd3f6f83): public, 39 BF16 shards, with all uploaded file hashes verified. The model card explains the inherited stale manifest and the scope of provenance checks. It received no updates from the degrading extended run. [Best related published merge and limitations](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-NUPA-BFCL-Shared100-2026.10.09/tree/462ad9af071055da39ef4bfea1d4ba2c9429a223) is a separate model.
- [Pinned MarinSkyRL runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/tree/fa6da4d8c67ed17b3fa69f689d9b444694683f8a), [pinned Harbor runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/436d0c92ed2fbb679438cd750e5fab3328153c31).
- Open follow-ups: [localized online feedback #10043](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043), [datakit single-turn comparison mining and DPO validation #10042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10042), and [complete online multi-harness RL integration #10041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10041).

## Decision Log

- Used offline preference learning while baseline task success remained low.
- Moved from Levanter to native MarinSkyRL DPO to exercise the unified trainer and periodic Pi evaluation.
- Stopped the extended run after degradation, preserving intermediate traces for analysis.
- Separated future behavioral interventions from the uncompleted online integration work.

## Conclusion

The performance and harness-robustness objectives remain unmet. The campaign leaves tested DPO plumbing and reusable collection/curation components, with three explicit follow-ups. Closing this issue archives the campaign; it does not certify successful recovery or complete online multi-harness RL.
